title: Marie de Médicis (Brulart) to Savary de Brèves, Rome, 15 Sept and 10 Nov 1610 (BnF fr. 3789)

steps.what: Located no. 12 in the scan: notice folios run two ahead of the stamped foliation; letter is stamped f. 19 (canvas 36).
Transcribed the 10 Nov passage and the 15 Sept sibling from full-resolution canvases.
Applied values from the interlinear-deciphered Villeroy 1605 letter in the same volume (f. 26).
Tomokiyo louisxiii.htm and DECODE: R2077 broken by Lasry/Biermann/Tomokiyo 2021; key in BnF fr. 3642, photo on R2077.
Read the 833-px key photo: alphabet, t-z box, codes 4-99, comma letter codes, barred 4-46; M-Z codes missing.
Beam search over each sign's candidate letters from the key reading, scored with fr-1600-letters.
Found Brèves's reply of 9 Dec 1610 to the 10 Nov letter (Cinq cents de Colbert 351, pp. 724-730); it paraphrases the Savoy/Spain points, no quotation of the ciphered words.

Brice Dudout (with Claude and Codex) located the key at BnF fr. 3462, Gallica btv1b9058227h view 112, and deciphered both passages with it by a manual glyph-by-glyph alignment (emails 16 and 19 Oct 2026).
Satoshi Tomokiyo confirmed to Brice that R2077's '3642' is a mistyping of fr. 3462 and corroborated barred 72 que, 79 re, 86 se, 90 tion (41 = leur).
Gallica IIIF returned 403 (Cloudflare); used the key image (1800 x 1580 px) and line crops from Brice's CC BY 4.0 repository.
Re-read our 21 Sept transcription against the key: bars on 72/79, 3ᵈ split, 'tu' one glyph; several of our letters lumped distinct key shapes.

Compared each of the 98 glyphs with the cell of view 112 it matches (alignment.tsv): 86 key, 3 probable, 6 off page (Tomokiyo), 3 conflict (re[c]ognoissant has b, one s without an S cell, acompagne[z] = E3 or Z2).
Settled three of Brice's brackets (am[b]ition, foi[b]lesse, [s]entant); proposed 'acompagnee' (E3) agreeing with 'ambition'.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Brice Dudout found that the Henri IV-Brèves key of 1610 (BnF fr. 3462 view 112, filed for another letter) fits Marie's passages and deciphered them; the project's sign-by-sign check finds 95 of 98 glyphs supported.
outcome.fraction_read_source: alignment.tsv, 98 cipher glyphs: 86 key + 3 probable + 6 Tomokiyo-corroborated = 95; 3 conflict counted as unread.

gaps.detail: B1 (b) on view 112; the word needs c. Regent's key or Lasry's R2077 decipherment needed.

gaps.item: 10 Nov second s of recognoissant, one sign
gaps.detail: No S cell on view 112 has this shape (closest A4).
E3 (e, 'acompagnee') or Z2 (z); the cells differ by a stroke.
N-Z page of the key not in hand; values as corroborated by Tomokiyo, counted as read.

credits.note: both passages deciphered with the fr. 3462 view 112 key (with Claude and Codex)
confirmed fr. 3462 (not 3642) and corroborated barred 72 que, 79 re, 86 se, 90 tion
credits.source: Tomokiyo's feedback to Brice Dudout, reported in his email of 19 Oct 2026

outcome.notes: Brice's reading checked against view 112: three brackets settled (b, b, s), 'acompagnee' proposed, re[c]ognoissant has a b sign. The 21 Sept attempt failed on an 833-px key photo and a transcription that merged distinct shapes.

prior.where: Tomokiyo (louisxiii.htm) and DECODE R2075/R2076: 'not deciphered'. Henri IV's own letter (R2077) was broken by Lasry, Biermann and Tomokiyo in 2021; its decryption is not on DECODE.

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.
